name: Timeline for Kitchen Backsplash Tile Installation: From Prep to Final Clean

step.name: Step 1: On-site measurement and wall inspection
step.text: Your installer inspects the drywall flatness, checks cabinet alignment, and reviews outlet placements across the kitchen walls. This step takes one to two hours and confirms whether drywall patching or electrical box adjustments are required before tile touches the wall.

step.name: Step 2: Wall preparation and electrical safety shutoff
step.text: The crew turns off power to kitchen circuits, removes outlet plates, degreases walls, and completes needed drywall leveling or repairs. Countertops and floors are covered with protective boards and drop cloths, usually taking two to four hours depending on drywall condition.

step.name: Step 3: Layout planning and dry-fitting
step.text: The installer establishes true level lines, marks centerlines over the cooktop, and dry-fits rows to balance cuts on cabinet ends. This planning phase takes about one to two hours and ensures no awkward tile slivers appear around outlets or under upper cabinets.

step.name: Step 4: Spreading adhesive and setting tile
step.text: Mortar is combed in small workable sections, tiles are set with uniform spacers, and edge trim is secured along exposed margins. Depending on the size of the kitchen and tile complexity, tile setting typically takes four to eight hours of focused work.

step.name: Step 5: Adhesive curing period
step.text: The thinset mortar requires a solid 24 hours to cure undisturbed under stable indoor temperatures before any grout is applied. During this waiting period, tile joints remain undisturbed so bonds achieve maximum strength without shifting.

step.name: Step 6: Grouting, haze cleanup, and perimeter caulking
step.text: Spacers are removed, grout is packed into joints, and tile faces are sponged clean to prevent haze. A color-matched flexible caulk bead seals the countertop-to-wall expansion gap, taking two to four hours before final inspection.
